title: The Blind Archer
text: An old archer sits on a stump with a bow across his knees, milk-white eyes turned to the sky. Around him stand the targets of every challenger he has beaten, each split dead centre. He has never lost, he says, and he would very much like a game.

options.label: The sharpest eye takes him on.

outcomes.text: They beat him by a hair. He laughs and gives them his quiver.
He wins, and gives them a lesson anyway.

options.label: The craftiest moves his target while he isn't looking.

outcomes.text: He hits it anyway, and does not offer a lesson.
He nods. Most people do. "Then a lesson for free," he says, and shows the Leader how he listens for where a thing will be.

options.label: Whoever carries a bow shoots against him.

outcomes.text: They lose, as everyone does, but by so little that he restrings their bow with his own string.
They lose by a mile. He laughs, and shows them why.
